ops.title: Real launchd drain-ladder timings, measured for the first time
ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-01 by daemonkit's first real-machine E2E. Nothing in the tree knew these; every
prior number came from an in-process fake.

**ExitTimeOut fires as designed.** A parked daemon over half-done work is removed by launchd at
6.005s / 6.019s / 6.020s / 6.028s against a 6s ExitTimeOut. Serve never returns; the flock is held
until SIGKILL.

**Daemon-side ladder edges, happy path:** serve.enter -> start.ready 44-382ms; drain.enter ->
drain.exit 5-14ms; close.enter -> close.exit 4-134ms. A whole clean ladder is ~250ms.

**Launcher verbs:** Ensure cold start 1.11-2.95s; converged no-op 15-91ms; upgrade 8.18-9.04s;
Control.Drain 255-256ms; launchd.Remove 37-55ms with the process gone 26ms later; SIGKILL -> gone
26ms.

**deploy:** Install 261ms; Activate 1.51-2.93s; Supersede 0.95-1.97s; re-Activate 0.98-1.56s;
Uninstall 0.76-0.92s; Reset 0.59-0.66s.

**ThrottleInterval=10 dominates every restart.** The 8.2-9.0s upgrade and the 9.66-9.69s post-kill
recovery are both throttle-bound, not daemonkit-bound. Budget at least 40s for any Ensure that
follows an exit — a timeout tuned against the in-process fakes will be far too tight.

One irreversible residue worth knowing: `loadOnce` runs `enable` on every install
(launchd/apply.go:272) and `Remove` never disables, so each label leaves a permanent row in
root-owned /var/db/com.apple.xpc.launchd/disabled.502.plist. No launchctl verb deletes a row and uid
502 cannot write the file. It is O(labels), not O(runs) — 6 rows across ~16 suite runs.
